meta.description: Curated government schemes relevant to women entrepreneurs in India.
meta.disclaimer: Scheme limits, interest rates and eligibility change. Always confirm on the official source link before applying.

fields.states: ['ALL'] for central schemes, otherwise the state names where it applies
fields.benefit_type: loan | subsidy | grant | guarantee | training | incubation | market_access
fields.social_groups: extra target groups: sc_st, obc, minority, rural, shg, artisan, street_vendor; empty = open to all women
fields.max_amount_inr: upper limit of financial support where one exists (null when not applicable)

schemes.name: Stand-Up India
schemes.summary: Bank loans between Rs 10 lakh and Rs 1 crore for women (and SC/ST) entrepreneurs setting up a new (greenfield) enterprise in manufacturing, services, trading or agri-allied activities.
eligibility: Woman entrepreneur aged 18 or above
Greenfield (first-time) enterprise
In a company or partnership, at least 51% stake held by a woman or SC/ST entrepreneur
Not in default to any bank or financial institution
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply online on the Stand-Up Mitra portal or directly at a scheduled commercial bank branch.
schemes.keywords: greenfield new enterprise manufacturing trading services bank loan composite term loan working capital

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY)
schemes.summary: Collateral-free loans for non-farm micro enterprises in four categories: Shishu (up to Rs 50,000), Kishore (Rs 50,000 to Rs 5 lakh), Tarun (Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh) and Tarun Plus (Rs 10 lakh to Rs 20 lakh, for those who repaid an earlier Tarun loan).
eligibility: Non-farm income-generating micro or small enterprise
Manufacturing, trading, services or activities allied to agriculture
No collateral required
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply at any bank, NBFC, MFI or through the JanSamarth portal.
schemes.keywords: micro loan shishu kishore tarun small shop tailoring beauty parlour food stall collateral free

schemes.name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)
schemes.summary: Credit-linked subsidy for new micro enterprises. Project cost up to Rs 50 lakh (manufacturing) or Rs 20 lakh (service). Women are a special category: 25% margin-money subsidy in urban areas and 35% in rural areas, with only 5% own contribution.
eligibility: Aged 18 or above
Class 8 pass for projects above Rs 10 lakh (manufacturing) or Rs 5 lakh (service)
New project only; existing units are not eligible
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply online on the KVIC PMEGP e-portal; applications are forwarded to banks.
schemes.keywords: margin money subsidy rural urban manufacturing service unit khadi village industries

schemes.name: Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)
schemes.summary: Guarantee cover that lets banks lend to micro and small enterprises without collateral or third-party guarantee. Women entrepreneurs receive higher guarantee coverage (85% for eligible loans) and a concession on the guarantee fee.
eligibility: Micro or small enterprise (manufacturing, services or retail trade)
Loan from a member lending institution
No collateral or third-party guarantee taken by the lender
schemes.how_to_apply: Ask your bank to cover the loan under CGTMSE when applying.
schemes.keywords: collateral free guarantee working capital term loan msme

schemes.name: PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PM FME)
schemes.summary: 35% credit-linked capital subsidy (up to Rs 10 lakh) for micro food-processing units, plus seed capital of up to Rs 40,000 per SHG member, training, branding and marketing support.
eligibility: Individual micro food-processing unit, SHG, FPO or cooperative
Applicant aged 18 or above with at least Class 8 education (individuals)
Ownership rights over the enterprise
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply on the PMFME portal; District Resource Persons help prepare the project report.
schemes.keywords: pickles papad spices millet bakery snacks food processing branding packaging odop

schemes.name: PM Vishwakarma
schemes.summary: Support for traditional artisans in 18 trades (e.g. tailoring, basket weaving, pottery, doll and toy making): skill training with stipend, a toolkit incentive of up to Rs 15,000, and collateral-free loans of Rs 1 lakh and Rs 2 lakh at 5% concessional interest.
eligibility: Artisan working with hands and tools in one of the 18 listed trades
Aged 18 or above
Not availed similar central or state credit schemes in the past five years
schemes.how_to_apply: Register at a Common Service Centre (CSC) through the PM Vishwakarma portal.
schemes.keywords: artisan tailor darzi basket mat pottery potter doll toy weaving traditional craft toolkit

schemes.name: PM SVANidhi (Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi)
schemes.authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
schemes.summary: Working-capital loans for urban street vendors in tranches of Rs 10,000, Rs 20,000 and Rs 50,000, with 7% interest subsidy and cashback for digital transactions.
eligibility: Street vendor in an urban area
Certificate of vending or identity card from the urban local body, or a letter of recommendation
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply on the PM SVANidhi portal or through a CSC or bank.
schemes.keywords: street vendor hawker cart stall vegetables fruits tea snacks working capital

schemes.name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS)
schemes.summary: Funding through selected incubators: grants of up to Rs 20 lakh for proof of concept and prototype, and up to Rs 50 lakh through convertible debentures or debt for market entry and commercialisation.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup, incorporated not more than two years before applying
Business idea using technology in its core product, service or business model
Not received more than Rs 10 lakh from other government schemes
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply on the Startup India Seed Fund portal and choose up to three incubators.
schemes.keywords: startup technology innovation prototype proof of concept incubator dpiit app platform

schemes.name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)
schemes.summary: Organises rural women into Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and provides revolving fund, community investment fund, bank linkage with interest subvention, skill training and market access (e.g. SARAS fairs). Supports the Lakhpati Didi initiative.
eligibility: Rural woman from a poor household
Member of (or willing to join) a Self-Help Group
schemes.how_to_apply: Contact the block-level office of the State Rural Livelihoods Mission or the village SHG federation.
schemes.keywords: self help group shg rural village livelihood lakhpati didi saras bank linkage

schemes.name: Mahila Samriddhi Yojana (NBCFDC)
schemes.authority: National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation
schemes.summary: Micro-finance for women from backward classes through State Channelising Agencies at concessional interest.
eligibility: Woman from a notified backward class
Annual family income within the limit notified by NBCFDC
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through the State Channelising Agency for NBCFDC in your state.
schemes.keywords: backward class obc micro finance concessional interest

schemes.name: NSFDC Mahila Samriddhi Yojana
schemes.authority: National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation
schemes.summary: Concessional micro-credit for women from Scheduled Castes to start small income-generating activities.
eligibility: Woman from a Scheduled Caste
Family income within the NSFDC limit
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through the State Channelising Agency for NSFDC.
schemes.keywords: scheduled caste sc micro credit concessional

schemes.name: NMDFC Micro Finance for Women (Mahila Samridhi)
schemes.authority: National Minorities Development and Finance Corporation
schemes.summary: Skill training followed by micro-credit for women from notified minority communities, routed through SHGs.
eligibility: Woman from a notified minority community
Member of an SHG
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through the State Channelising Agency for NMDFC.
schemes.keywords: minority muslim christian sikh buddhist jain parsi micro credit shg tailoring embroidery

schemes.name: MSME Champions & Udyam Registration (Udyam Assist for informal enterprises)
schemes.summary: Free Udyam registration gives access to priority-sector lending, public procurement preference (3% of central procurement is reserved for women-owned MSEs), and most MSME schemes.
eligibility: Micro, small or medium enterprise with Aadhaar of the proprietor/partner
Informal micro enterprises can register through Udyam Assist
schemes.how_to_apply: Register free of cost on the Udyam Registration portal.
schemes.keywords: udyam registration msme certificate government procurement gem tender priority sector

schemes.name: GeM Womaniya
schemes.summary: Lets women entrepreneurs and women SHGs sell handicrafts, handlooms, accessories, office supplies and services directly to government buyers on GeM.
eligibility: Woman-owned enterprise or women SHG
Udyam registration and PAN
schemes.how_to_apply: Register as a seller on gem.gov.in and select the Womaniya category.
schemes.keywords: government buyers sell online marketplace handloom jute office supplies

schemes.name: Women Entrepreneurship Platform (WEP)
schemes.summary: Aggregator platform for women entrepreneurs: mentorship, incubation and acceleration programmes, funding connections, compliance help and community.
eligibility: Any aspiring or existing woman entrepreneur
schemes.how_to_apply: Sign up on the WEP portal.
schemes.keywords: mentorship network incubation accelerator community guidance

schemes.name: SAMARTH – Scheme for Capacity Building in Textile Sector
schemes.summary: Free demand-driven, placement-oriented skill training in garmenting, handloom, handicrafts and allied textile trades. A large share of trainees are women.
eligibility: Aged 18 or above
Interest in textile or apparel work
schemes.how_to_apply: Enrol through a SAMARTH implementing partner listed on the portal.
schemes.keywords: tailoring stitching garment apparel embroidery handloom skill training

schemes.name: WE Hub – Telangana State Women Entrepreneurs Hub
schemes.summary: India's first state-led incubator exclusively for women entrepreneurs. Runs incubation, acceleration and rural programmes, and connects founders with investors, mentors and government departments.
eligibility: Woman-founded or woman-led business or idea
Programme-specific criteria apply
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply to an open programme on the WE Hub website.
schemes.keywords: hyderabad incubator accelerator women founders mentorship investors rural

schemes.name: Stree Nidhi Credit Cooperative Federation
schemes.summary: Quick, low-documentation credit for members of women SHGs for livelihood and income-generating activities, delivered through village organisations.
eligibility: Member of an SHG in Telangana
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through your SHG and village organisation.
schemes.keywords: shg village organisation quick credit rural telangana livelihood

schemes.name: T-PRIDE (Telangana State Program for Rapid Incubation of Dalit Entrepreneurs)
schemes.summary: Capital investment subsidy, interest subsidy and other incentives for SC/ST entrepreneurs, with additional subsidy percentages for women.
eligibility: SC/ST entrepreneur setting up an enterprise in Telangana
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through the TS-iPASS portal of the Industries Department.
schemes.keywords: scheduled caste tribe dalit capital subsidy interest subsidy telangana industries

schemes.name: Andhra Pradesh MSME incentives for women entrepreneurs
schemes.authority: Government of Andhra Pradesh, Industries Department
schemes.summary: The state industrial policy provides additional investment subsidy, power-cost reimbursement and stamp-duty concessions for MSMEs owned by women.
eligibility: Woman-owned MSME in Andhra Pradesh
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through the AP Single Desk portal.
schemes.keywords: andhra pradesh industrial policy investment subsidy power reimbursement stamp duty

schemes.name: Udyogini
schemes.summary: Bank loans of up to Rs 3 lakh for women to start small businesses, with a subsidy component that is higher for SC/ST women.
eligibility: Woman aged 18 to 55 in Karnataka
Family income within the notified limit
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply at the district office of the Karnataka State Women's Development Corporation.
schemes.keywords: karnataka small business loan subsidy women development corporation

schemes.name: NEEDS – New Entrepreneur-cum-Enterprise Development Scheme
schemes.authority: Government of Tamil Nadu, MSME Department
schemes.summary: Entrepreneurship training plus capital subsidy and interest subvention for first-generation entrepreneurs, with a higher share reserved for women.
eligibility: First-generation entrepreneur in Tamil Nadu
Graduate, diploma or ITI qualification
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply online through the MSME Tamil Nadu portal.
schemes.keywords: first generation entrepreneur capital subsidy tamil nadu

schemes.name: Kudumbashree Micro Enterprises
schemes.authority: Kudumbashree State Poverty Eradication Mission, Kerala
schemes.summary: Support for women's neighbourhood-group enterprises: start-up funds, revolving funds, training, branding and markets such as Kudumbashree bazaars and cafes.
eligibility: Member of a Kudumbashree neighbourhood group in Kerala
schemes.how_to_apply: Contact the local Community Development Society (CDS).
schemes.keywords: kerala neighbourhood group cafe catering bazaar micro enterprise

schemes.name: Punyashlok Ahilyadevi Holkar Women Startup Scheme
schemes.summary: Financial assistance of Rs 1 lakh to Rs 25 lakh for early-stage women-led startups registered in Maharashtra.
eligibility: DPIIT-recognised startup registered in Maharashtra
At least 50% shareholding held by women founders
Annual turnover within the scheme limit
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply when the call for applications opens on the MSInS website.
schemes.keywords: maharashtra women startup grant msins innovation

schemes.name: Kerala Startup Mission – Women Startup Support
schemes.summary: Innovation grants, incubation and special support (including soft loans against government purchase orders) for women-led startups in Kerala.
eligibility: Startup registered with Kerala Startup Mission
Woman founder or co-founder
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through the KSUM portal.
schemes.keywords: kerala startup innovation grant incubation ksum
